subject: Archaeology
title: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon
description: Learn The Hanging Gardens of Babylon in one minute.

hook.text: The Hanging Gardens were one of the Seven Wonders. But no one has found any trace of them — and Babylon's own records.

buildup.text: Greek writers described terraced gardens watered by ingenious screws, built by King Nebuchadnezzar for his homesick.

discovery.text: German archaeologists excavated Babylon for 18 years starting in 1899. They found the Ishtar Gate — but no gardens.

twist.text: Stephanie Dalley argues the gardens were actually at Nineveh, built by the Assyrian king Sennacherib — not.

climax.text: Reliefs at Nineveh show lush gardens watered by aqueducts. The wonder may have existed — just in the wrong city.

punchline.text: The most famous garden in history may have been real — just 300 miles from.

quiz.question: What is Stephanie Dalley's theory about the Hanging Gardens?
options: They were entirely fictional, created by Greek writers for propaganda
They were actually at Nineveh, built by the Assyrian king Sennacherib
They existed at Babylon but were destroyed by Alexander the Great
